about.title: Burlingame Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Burlingame saw 3 traffic deaths among its 104 injury collisions in the most recent year of final data, and behind each number is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss. California law gives certain surviving family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some situations. These cases sit apart from any criminal proceedings and focus instead on the financial and emotional toll left behind: funeral and burial costs, lost income and support the person would have provided, and the loss of their guidance and companionship. Corridors like US-101, California Drive, and SR-82 see steady traffic volume, and Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. tend to show more reported crashes locally. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect grieving families with an independent attorney who can walk through the options, free of charge, so you're not left figuring out deadlines and paperwork alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Families in Burlingame Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Understanding Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific family members, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then extending to certain dependents or heirs. An independent attorney can help sort out who in your family qualifies before decisions get made.

items.title: A Firm Deadline That Doesn't Wait
items.desc: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Getting connected early helps preserve records and evidence tied to the incident.

items.title: Losses Beyond Medical Bills
items.desc: Wrongful death recoveries in California can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love and guidance. These are separate from any criminal case tied to the same crash.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California law generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children. If none of those exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing to bring the claim. An independent attorney can review your family's specific situation to clarify who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing a family member in Burlingame?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to bring a wrongful death claim. That window shrinks considerably if a government entity, like a public road authority, may share responsibility. Because Burlingame's busiest corridors include state routes like SR-82, it's worth having this checked promptly.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect us with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. Our role is simply to help your family reach the right attorney without added cost or pressure.
